(A,B) The figure depicts the histopathological findings from a skin biopsy obtained during the patient's admission. (A) Demonstrates the dermis extensively infiltrated by sheets of foamy histiocytes, characterized by their pale, vacuolated cytoplasm. Notably, well-formed granulomas are absent in this specimen (yellow arrow).

(A,B) The figure depicts the histopathological findings from a skin biopsy obtained during the patient's admission. (B) Highlights the results of an acid-fast stain, revealing a dense population of acid-fast bacilli packed within the foamy macrophages, a hallmark feature indicative of lepromatous leprosy (depicted with circles).
Facial hypomimia and left-sided facial paresis (arrow), consistent with the involvement of the facial nerve in Hansen's disease.
Anterior chest, and.

posterior trunk prior to initiation of ROM therapy. Multiple erythematous, edematous plaques with central clearing are present, consistent with active lepromatous leprosy (LL). Images courtesy of the treating dermatologist. Patient consent was obtained for publication. Non-relevant skin markings (nevi) were obscured to prevent patient identification; leprosy lesions remain unaltered.
Anterior chest, and.

posterior trunk approximately 6 weeks after initiation of ROM therapy. Partial resolution of erythema and reduction in plaque thickness are observed, demonstrating early clinical improvement. Images courtesy of the treating dermatologist. Patient consent was obtained for publication. Anterior chest, and.

posterior trunk approximately 8 months after initiation of ROM therapy. Marked improvement with near-complete resolution of plaques and minimal residual erythema is evident, consistent with sustained treatment response. Images courtesy of the treating dermatologist. Patient consent was obtained for publication. Non-relevant skin markings (moles) were obscured to prevent patient identification; leprosy lesions remain unaltered.
